note: Synthetic interaction traces. Rust verifies every state and effect. swift_reference cases compare existing HoverCoordinator and EdgeHubNavigation projections only; tagged timer callback injection, visibility/focus policy and native windows are not Swift parity claims. Fixture timestamps are monotonic milliseconds, not wall time.

cases.note: The detail survives travel into its card; leaving the card dismisses after the existing 250 ms delay. Swift checks actual HoverCoordinator outcomes.
A stale exit or cancelled timer cannot replace a newer hover. Pinned content resists hover; explicit activation changes the pin.
Hide clears transient interaction state; callbacks from before hide cannot dismiss newly pinned details. Swift reference covers hover/navigation projections only.
Escape follows the same review/client/home and setup/connection/home hierarchy as EdgeHubNavigation; closing a card allows idle folding.
Outside click dismisses details or settings without immediately folding. A new pointer visit resumes ordinary idle folding. Swift checks only the dismissed core models.
Equal-time batches prioritize observations over callbacks regardless of callback position; repeated reopen replaces an old fold deadline.
Observed keyboard focus holds the corresponding surface open. Losing focus resumes delayed dismissal and folding.
Settings remains open through transient focus loss and keyboard traversal. Closing its last page requests native widget focus without pretending focus was granted.
Native enter-before-exit delivery cannot clear the new pointer region; hovering the settings handle prevents idle folding.
Always-visible mode cancels idle folding. Visibility commands are in-memory only; native preference persistence belongs to the shell.
An early callback retains its original deadline; unknown and duplicate tokens cannot create or dismiss UI.
Hidden widgets reject late pointer/focus/click observations; same-batch Hide invalidates earlier focus requests.
Menu, keyboard and accessibility activation use the same explicit actions. Hover cannot replace pins; opening settings clears details.
Input order is stable within a batch, all earlier callbacks become stale, and a focus request for a card hidden in that batch is discarded.
Escape requests focus back to the widget; an outside click clears focus without requesting it back or stealing focus from another application.

Keyboard/menu/accessibility unpin with the pointer outside cancels dismissal and retains the selected card until a later metric/card leave, matching Swift togglePin. A cancelled callback in the unpin batch cannot dismiss the card.
